summary: FeeHub receipt geometry + preview + settings flow fully verified. /print-lab receipt frame measures widthMm=209.9965 and scrollHeightMm=142.3458 (target <= 142.8mm), fits with no overflow. Layout matches reference: BALAJI CONVENT header + Marathi Primary School, black FEE RECEIPT box + tagline, RECEIPT NO/DATE/ACADEMIC YEAR, barcode, DETAILS 2-col grid (student left / parent+meta right), fee table on left with SR.NO/FEE HEAD/TOTAL/PAID/BALANCE + TOTAL row, payment panel on right (AMOUNT IN WORDS/PAYMENT MODE/TRANSACTION ID/AMOUNT RECEIVED big rupee), notes, RECEIVED BY / AUTHORIZED BY, bottom contact bar. No 'Balance Remaining' ribbon, nothing clipped. Settings page shows Receipt Printer card with all required data-testids, media defaults to A5, Save + Print Test Receipt opens the FeeHub Print Preview modal rendered by the SAME renderer at identical geometry (widthMm=209.9965, heightMm=142.7965, scrollHeightMm=142.3458). No navigation to a receipt page and no receipt/payment is created. Clicking rv-print-direct in the preview shows inline error 'Direct receipt printing is not yet available on this build.' and the modal remains open — this is the expected browser (no Electron/window.feehub IPC) behavior. Backend GET /api/receipt-types with admin bearer returns exactly 9 codes: BUS, DV, EMJC, EMP, EP, JC, JCACS, MP, SEC.

minor.issue: Administrator accounts are hard-blocked from remote login (403 'Administrator accounts can only sign in from the Main Server itself, not over the network.'). This is by-design for the Electron desktop shell (see routers/auth.py L22-24), but it means the review request statement 'Admin login works ... in browser' does not literally hold in this k8s preview — testing had to inject a locally-issued bearer token into localStorage.bc_token to reach /settings. If admin flows are ever expected to be verifiable in the preview URL directly, this local-IP guard needs a preview-env allowance. No functional bug.

critical_code_review_comments: Admin-remote-login guard in backend/routers/auth.py L22-24 relies on is_server_local_request which compares request.client.host to the pod's local IPs — behind a k8s ingress the client host is typically an internal proxy IP, so the effect is that admin can never log in over any deployed URL. Fine if the product is ONLY ever run on the operator's own workstation (Electron), but ensure QA/preview envs have a documented bypass (e.g. localhost/curl) instead of appearing as an auth bug.
